subject: Continuous coverage proposal & burn-rate discount conversation
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightcart.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: continuous 24/7 coverage + burn-rate discount

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightCart is very interested in Redwood's Dedicated offering. We're approaching renewal for our inference footprint in Q4 and procurement asked me to scope a couple of commercial options before we lock dates with infra. Two asks: 

1) Can you provide a short proposal for a "continuous coverage" SLA add-on (24/7 escalation coverage across PST/EST/EU windows) with concrete pricing tiers and what constitutes an "incident" for crediting?

2) We saw you mention "burn-rate discounts" in the deck. If we commit to a 12-month minimum spend (committed tokens / GPU hours), what discount band might apply to premium SLA add-ons vs. pay-as-you-go?

We have an internal doc with rough monthly consumption — I'll attach a sanitized sample if helpful. Ideally procurement wants a simple table: coverage band, response times, monthly price, and discount for 12m commit.

Can you send something for review by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Ethan
Senior Ops Manager, BrightCart

Attachment: usage-sample-agg.csv (sanitized sample of monthly token & peak concurrent requests)
From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: continuous 24/7 coverage + burn-rate discount

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the sample. High level proposal below (I'll follow up with a one-page addendum PDF):

Summary (short):
- Continuous Coverage Add-on: 24/7 escalation with a named on-call rotation, global runbook alignment, and guaranteed triage within the listed response windows.
- Two coverage bands: "Core (business hours)" and "Continuous (24/7)". Core covers M-F 08:00-18:00 local, Continuous covers full 24/7 with SRE escalation.
- Incident definition: sustained customer-impacting service degradation for >5 minutes OR error-rate >3x baseline for 3 consecutive sampling windows (we'll include metric thresholds in the addendum).

Proposed pricing (monthly, US region):
- Core band: $6,500/mo — 6 business-hour triage + standard SLA credits
- Continuous band: $18,000/mo — named on-call, 60-min followup for P2, 15-min for P1, direct Slack escalation channel

Burn-rate / commit discount guidance (12m CCP = committed consumption plan):
- No commit (pay-as-you-go): add-on listed price above
- 12m commit >= $500k TCV: 10% off add-on price
- 12m commit >= $1M TCV: 18% off add-on price + 1 free on-call training session / year

Deliverables we'll attach: short addendum PDF, proposed SLA metrics excerpt, DocuSign-ready addendum.

Questions for you to finalize numbers:
- Can you confirm the expected 95th percentile concurrency and monthly token burn from the sample?
- Are there any regulatory constraints requiring local on-prem SRE presence?

I'll loop Ben and Kim for the small legal/pricing caveats. If that looks directionally correct I can produce the addendum and a simple two-row DocuSign for procurement.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: BrightCart_SLA_Rolling_Addendum_v1.pdf (stub)
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: continuous 24/7 coverage + burn-rate discount

Noted a couple of commercial points to tighten before sending to procurement:

1) Discount phasing: recommend making the midpoint band clearer — e.g., for $500k–$999k TCV, 12% (not 10) to reduce back-and-forth. Buyers anchor against a single discount line; a modest bump helps close.
2) Credit calculation: define credits as % of monthly add-on fee (P1 incident = 25% credit, P2 = 10% credit) — this keeps math predictable in procurement comparisons.
3) Regional failover: add a capped regional failover surcharge (one-time) if BrightCart requires guaranteed on-prem shadowing or HSM presence.

I'll draft a short table and swap into Lauren's addendum. Also, include a clause that discounts apply only to the add-on, not base inference usage, unless they want to roll the full committed spend into a blended discount — that requires a different deal team.

Ben
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@brightcart.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Request: continuous 24/7 coverage + burn-rate discount

Lauren / Ben — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clarity. Procurement flagged two final items before we proceed to DocuSign: 

1) Can you convert the credit amounts into a worked example (assume one P1 and two P2 incidents in a month) so our CFO can see net expected cost difference vs. no-add-on?
2) We'd prefer the 12m commit to apply to the combined spend (inference + SLA add-on) — can you provide a one-row example of blended pricing for our CFO (use the $1M TCV band)?

If you can send the worked examples and the DocuSign link early next week, procurement will route for approval. We're aligned on the Continuous band.

Thanks,
Ethan
